blocks.text: Network performance means how well a network works: the speed and quality of data transfer. Good performance gives fast, smooth communication; poor performance causes slow Internet and delays. Performance depends on many factors, such as bandwidth and latency.

blocks.caption: Bandwidth and latency
rows: The amount of data that can be sent in a given time: how much data the network can carry
The time data takes to travel: the delay between sending and receiving
Low bandwidth, or many devices sharing it, makes the Internet slow
High latency causes lag; online games and video calls need low latency

blocks.title: Bandwidth and actual speed
blocks.text: Strictly, bandwidth is the maximum rate a link can carry; the rate actually achieved, called throughput, is often lower because the link is shared and because of delays and errors.

items: Too many users on the network.

blocks.title: Class activity
blocks.text: Identify the possible causes of delay in a given scenario.

blocks.prompt: A video call keeps freezing even though a large file downloads quickly. Is the problem more likely bandwidth or latency? Explain.
blocks.explanation: Latency (delay). The fast download shows bandwidth is enough; a live video call needs each packet to arrive quickly, so high or varying delay makes it freeze.

items: Performance: speed and quality of data transfer.
Bandwidth: data per unit time (Mbps), higher is better; latency: delay (ms), lower is better.
Delay causes: many users, poor cables, distance, congestion, hardware faults.
